title: The Silver-Wood Raft to the Harbor of Dreams
verses:
As the twilight descended on Meadowlark Glade,
Little Rory brought pinecones to rest in the shade.
Gentle Tilly wove blankets of moss soft and deep,
While Benny swept pathways to welcome their sleep.

Then Ricky brought lanterns of dew-covered glass,
Which glowed with a hum in the whispering grass.
Nia polished the petals of moon-lilies white,
That opened to drink in the velvet of night.

Psittaco sang softly a silver-toned song,
That floated through willow trees all evening long.
They boarded a raft made of silver-wood bark,
To drift on the stream as it glided past dark.

The river rolled gently as smooth as a glass,
Where small glowing goldfish would quietly pass.
Rory rested his head on a pillow of down,
As Tilly watched fireflies flicker around.

With Benny and Ricky tucked under the sail,
And Nia fast asleep by the soft wooden rail,
Psittaco tucked wings with a satisfied sigh,
Beneath the pale glow of the lullaby sky.

The raft floated slow to the Harbor of Dreams,
Carried safely away on the calmest of streams.
So close your sweet eyes as the darkness descends,
Goodnight to young Rory and all of his friends.
